raw_text:
Here’s the consolidated 12-week plan summary for your advanced lifter at 20 weeks pregnant. It integrates strength (3 days/week + optional Day D), intensified Phase 2, robust pressing emphasis, cardio, core, and pregnancy-specific nutrition and safety. All sessions avoid supine work, max attempts, and Valsalva; use RPE and breath quality to guide load.

Global anchors
- Frequency: 3 lifting days (A Lower, B Upper, C Total/Power-Stability) + optional Day D (Mobility/Core/LISS).
- Intensity: Compounds RPE 6–7 most weeks; select top sets up to RPE 8 in Phase 2. Accessories RPE 6–8. Always 2–3 reps in reserve; stop sets on coning, pelvic pressure, pain, dizziness, or breath-hold.
- Breathing/bracing: 360-breathing; “exhale before/through exertion.” No prolonged breath holds.
- Positions: No flat supine. Use incline 30–45°, seated, standing, half/tall-kneeling, quadruped, side-lying. Favor unilateral/supported work as bump grows.
- Progression: Add 1 rep or 2.5–5% weekly if RPE ≤7 and symptom-free. Deload Weeks 4, 8; Peak-style Week 12 with safe heavy exposures (no 1RMs).
- Warm-up each session: 3–5 min breathing/PF priming + 5–8 min dynamic mobility.

Phase 1 (Weeks 1–4): Foundation and maintenance (gestational ~20–23)
Goal: Maintain strength/technique; introduce incline/supported variations; core/PF coordination.
- Week 1
  - Day A Lower: Safety bar box squat 4x5 RPE 6–7; Trap bar DL (high handles) 4x4 RPE 6–7; RFESS 3x8/side RPE 7; 45° back extension 2x10 RPE 6; Half-kneeling Pallof 2x10/side.
  - Day B Upper (pressing focus): Incline barbell bench 4x6 RPE 6–7; Chest-supported 1-arm DB row 4x8/side RPE 7; Half-kneeling landmine press 3x8/side RPE 7; Lat pulldown neutral 3x10; Side-lying hip abduction/clams 2x12/side; Add F: Incline push-up 3x8–12 RPE 6–7.
  - Day C Total/Power: KB swing 6x10 on 60–75 s RPE 6 (or cable pull-through 4x12 if symptoms); Front-foot elevated split squat 3x8/side; Chest-supported rear-delt fly 3x12; Tall-kneeling anti-rotation press 3x10/side; Farmer carry 4x20–30 m.
  - Core add (post-lift): 90/90 breathing 2x5/side; Half-kneeling Pallof 2x10/side; Quadruped rock-back 2x8.
  - Cardio: 2–3 sessions steady Z1–Z2, 20–25 min.
- Week 2
  - Progress loads slightly; same structure. Add F: Single-arm cable press 3x10/side on Upper Day.
  - Core: 90/90 2x5/side; Standing Pallof 3x8/side; Bird-dog short lever 2x6/side.
  - Cardio: 3 sessions 20–25 min steady.
- Week 3
  - Day A: SSB box squat 5x4 RPE 7; Trap bar DL 5x3 RPE 7.
  - Day B: Incline bench 5x5 RPE 6–7; Rows/landmine slightly heavier; Add F: Seated DB shoulder press 3x8 RPE 7.
  - Day C: Maintain volume; progress 1 rep or 2–3%.
  - Core: Seated 360 breaths 1x6; Tall-kneeling anti-rotation 3x8/side; Side bridge from bench 2x20–30 s/side.
- Week 4 Deload
  - Main lifts 3x4 RPE ~6; accessories 2x8–10; tempo control 3–0–2.
  - Upper pressing: Incline press 3x5 RPE 6; Landmine 2x8/side; Cable fly 2x12.
  - Core easy: 90/90 2x5; Pallof hold 2x20–30 s/side; Bird-dog 2x5/side.
  - Cardio: 2 easy Z1–Z2, 20–22 min.

Phase 2 (Weeks 5–8): Intensified but safe (gestational ~24–27)
Goal: Strong training feel via top sets, clusters/EMOMs, density blocks; manage posture and symmetry; keep RPE ceilings.
- Week 5
  - Day A Lower: Hatfield squat to box—Top 1x4 @RPE 8; back-offs 3x4 @7. DB RDL 4x6 @7–8; Step-downs 3x10/side @7; Density 8–10 min: Cable pull-through 10 + Banded lateral walk 12/side.
  - Day B Upper (pressing focus strong): Incline DB bench—Top 1x6 @8; 3x6 @7. Chest-supported T-bar row 4x8 @7–8; Half-kneeling landmine press 4x6/side @7–8; Pulldown 3x10 @7; Density 6–8 min: Incline push-up 8–12 + Single-arm cable press 10/side.
  - Day C Total/Power: Trap bar from blocks—Cluster 4x(2+2) @RPE 7; Split squat (suitcase) 3x8/side @7–8; Single-arm cable row 3x10/side @7; Farmer carry 4x25–30 m.
  - Core (post-lift): Pallof to overhead raise 3x8/side; Incline dead bug (arms + opposite heel slide) 3x6–8/side; Suitcase carry 3x25–30 m/side.
  - Cardio: Intervals Session 1—8x1 min @RPE 6–7 + 2 min easy (bike/elliptical); Session 2—Z2 25–30 min; Session 3—Recovery 20–25 min.
- Week 6
  - Strength: Progress top sets 2.5–5% if clean; maintain structure.
  - Upper press main: Incline barbell or machine—Top 1x5–6 @8; 3x5–6 @7. Landmine press 4x6/side heavier. Add F: Seated DB Arnold press 3x8 @7.
  - Core: Tall-kneeling anti-rotation slow eccentric 3x8/side; Incline dead bug 3x8/side; Marching cable row iso 2x10–12 marches/side.
  - Cardio Session 1—6x2 min @RPE 6–7 + 2 min easy; Session 2—Z2 25–30; Session 3—Recovery.
- Week 7
  - Day A: Hatfield—Top 1x3 @8; 4x3 @7–7.5; DB RDL 4x6–7 @7–8; Single-leg leg press 3x10/side @7–8; Pull-through 3x12.
  - Day B: Machine or incline DB—Top 1x5 @8; 3x5 @7; Landmine 3x8/side @7; Row/pulldown as programmed; Pec deck/cable fly 3x12 @7; Optional eccentric incline push-up 2x6–8 (3–4 s down).
  - Day C: Trap bar blocks—EMOM 10 min: 2 reps @RPE 6–7; Reverse lunge (slider) 3x8/side @7–8; Anti-rotation press 3x10/side; Farmer carry 4x30 m.
  - Core: Pallof step-out 3x6 steps/side; Bird-dog with roller 3x6/side; Tall-kneeling band pulldown 2x10.
  - Cardio: Pyramid 1–2–3–2–1 @RPE 6–7 with equal easy + 5–8 min Z2; Uphill walk 25–30 min; Recovery 20–25 min.
- Week 8 Deload/Consolidate
  - Volume −30–40%, RPE 6–6.5 on mains; accessories 2x8–10 @6–7.
  - Upper pressing: Incline 3x5 @6–6.5; Landmine 2x8/side @6; Cable fly 2x12 light.
  - Core easy: 90/90 2x5; Pallof hold 2x20 s/side; Rock-back 2x6.
  - Cardio: 2 easy Z1–Z2 sessions, 20–25 min.

Phase 3 (Weeks 9–12): Comfort, stability, expression (gestational ~28–31)
Goal: Keep strength quality, reduce axial peaks, favor machines/support; prepare for peak-style Week 12 without true maxing.
- Week 9
  - Day A Lower: Leg press 4x8 @6–7; DB RDL with wall support 4x6–8; Step-up low box 3x8/side; Cable pull-through or banded hip thrust 3x12; Standing Pallof 3x10/side.
  - Day B Upper: Seated machine chest press or incline DB 4x6–8 @7; Seated DB OHP neutral 3x8 @7 (swap to landmine if needed); Chest-supported row 4x8; Lat pulldown 3x10–12; Rear-delt machine 2x12–15; Incline push-up 2–3x8–12 easy-moderate.
  - Day C Total: Trap bar from blocks 4x3–4 @6–7; Split squat 3x8/side; Single-arm cable row 3x10/side; Suitcase/offset carry 4x20 m/side.
  - Core: Standing Pallof 3x8/side; Incline dead bug 2–3x6/side; Suitcase carry easy-moderate.
  - Cardio: 2–3 sessions, favor pool/recumbent bike, 20–30 min, RPE 3–5.
- Week 10
  - Maintain/microload 1–2% if symptom-free; swap step-ups for single-leg press if balance wanes; add adductor/abductor machine 2x12 each if desired.
  - Core: Tall-kneeling anti-rotation 3x8/side; Bird-dog short lever 2–3x5/side; Tall-kneeling band pulldown 2x10.
  - Cardio: Maintain frequency; mostly Z2; one bike with 4x4 min @RPE 5–6 if energy good.
- Week 11
  - Day A: Leg press 5x6 @7; Wall-supported DB RDL 4x8; Reverse lunge 3x8/side; Pull-through 3x12.
  - Day B: Incline DB bench 4x6–8 @7; Landmine press half-kneeling 3x8/side; Chest-supported row 4x8; Neutral pulldown 3x10–12; Face pulls 2x15.
  - Day C: Trap bar blocks 4x3 @6–7; Step-ups or single-leg press 3x10/side; Anti-rotation press 3x10/side; Farmer/rack carry 4x20 m.
  - Core: Pallof step-out 2x5 steps/side; Incline dead bug arms-only 2x8; Marching cable row iso 2x8 marches/side.
  - Cardio: Maintain; 1 session with 4x4 min @RPE 5–6; others easy.
- Week 12 Peak-style (no 1RMs)
  - Day A “heavy exposures”: Hatfield or Leg Press—2–3 singles @RPE 7–8 (clean speed); Back-off 2x4 @~80% of day’s single @RPE ~7. Trap bar blocks 3x2 @RPE 7; Split squat 2x8/side @7; Pallof 2x10/side.
  - Day B Upper press “peak”: Incline press (barbell/DB/machine)—2–3 singles @RPE 7–8; Back-off 2x5 @RPE 7. Landmine press 3x6/side @7; Chest-supported row 3x8 @7; Face pull 2x12 light.
  - Day C Technique/flow: Trap bar blocks EMOM 4x2 @RPE 6–7; FFE split squat 2x8/side; Single-arm cable row 2x10/side; Suitcase carry 3x20 m/side.
  - Optional cap-set after A1 on Days A/B: 1 set at a load you could do 8–10 reps; stop at 6 reps or RPE 8 to estimate e1RM safely.
  - Core (light): 90/90 breathing 2x5; Standing Pallof 2x8/side; Side-lying TVA 2x5 breaths.
  - Cardio: Deload—2 easy Z1–Z2 sessions 20–25 min; gentle walks.
  - Post-peak: 3–4 easy recovery days before resuming.

Cardio summary (weeks 1–12)
- Phase 1: 2–3x/week steady 20–30 min (talk-test).
- Phase 2: 2 structured + 1 recovery
  - W5: 8x1 min @RPE 6–7 + 2 min easy; Z2 25–30; Recovery 20–25.
  - W6: 6x2 min @RPE 6–7 + 2 min easy; Z2; Recovery.
  - W7: Pyramid 1–2–3–2–1 @RPE 6–7 + Z2; Uphill walk; Recovery.
  - W8: Deload—2 easy Z1–Z2 20–25.
- Phase 3: Comfort-priority—pool/bike/treadmill 20–30 min, RPE 3–5; one moderate session (e.g., 4x4 min @RPE 5–6) in W10–11 if energy is good.

Core summary (rotate per weeks above; 2–3 drills post-lift, 2–3 sets, RPE 6–7)
- Staples: 90/90 breathing; Pallof variations; Incline dead bug; Bird-dog (short lever); Side bridge on bench; Tall/half-kneeling chops/lifts; Suitcase carries; High-incline bear hover; Marching cable row iso.
- Rules: Avoid supine/sit-ups/rollouts; stop at first sign of coning/heaviness; prioritize quality and breathing.

Pressing emphasis summary
- Weekly: One strong incline press (barbell/DB/machine) with top set/back-offs in Phase 2; one landmine or seated DB press; push-up/cable fly accessories as tolerated.
- RPE ceilings: Top sets to 8 in Phase 2; maintain 6–7 elsewhere. Swap to machine if arching/balance uncomfortable.

Nutrition summary for lean mass and pregnancy support
- Calories: +250–350 kcal/day in 2nd tri; +350–450 kcal/day as 3rd tri approaches; adjust ±100–150 kcal based on OB-guided weight gain, energy, and performance.
- Macros:

Emphasis is on maintaining strength, postural integrity, pelvic floor health, and preparing for the biomechanical changes of pregnancy. - Intensity/loading: RPE 6–7 most strength work; accessories RPE 6–8. Avoid grinding reps, no reps in reserve fewer than 2–3. Stop sets if breath-holding or form breakdown appears.
- Tempo/bracing: Exhale on exertion; avoid prolonged breath holds/Valsalva. Use 2–0–2 or 3–0–2 tempos to control intra-abdominal pressure (IAP).
- Positions: No supine after week 16. Use incline (30–45°), half-kneeling, tall-kneeling, seated, or standing. Prefer unilateral and supported variations as bump grows.

- Pelvic floor: Integrate coordinated “exhale-to-exert” and gentle pelvic floor contractions and full relaxations. Include down-training (relaxation) as well as activation.
- Rest: 60–120s between main sets; 45–75s on accessories. Longer rests if symptomatic.
- Red flags (stop/modify and refer if needed): dizziness, vaginal bleeding, leaking amniotic fluid, chest pain, calf swelling, persistent headache, regular painful contractions, unusual shortness of breath, decreased fetal movement, pubic symphysis or sharp pelvic pain.
- Progression: Add load or 1 rep per set weekly if RPE ≤7 and no symptoms. If symptoms or excessive fatigue, hold or regress 5–10%.
- Deload: Week 4, 8, and 12 are built-in reloads or performance consolidations with reduced volume/intensity.

1) Breathing/pelvic floor priming 3–5 minutes

Here’s a practical, pregnancy-focused nutrition plan to help your client maintain lean mass while supporting a healthy pregnancy. It complements the 12-week training program and is meant to be individualized with her OB/midwife and, ideally, a registered dietitian.

Principles
- Prioritize adequate calories, high-quality protein, and steady carbs to fuel training and support fetal growth.
- Emphasize micronutrient-rich whole foods; keep hydration high; avoid overheating and excessive stimulants.
- Aim for gradual, guideline-consistent weight gain per OB guidance.

Calorie targets
- Second trimester: typically +250–350 kcal/day above pre-pregnancy maintenance.
- Third trimester (toward end of this 12-week block): +350–450 kcal/day above pre-pregnancy maintenance.
- Practical approach:
  - If she knows her maintenance: add the ranges above and track weekly weight gain and energy.
  - If not: start around 30–33 kcal/kg current body weight, then adjust by 100–150 kcal every 1–2 weeks based on:
    - Energy, training performance, satiety
    - Weight gain aligned with OB targets (often ~0.35–0.5 kg/week in 2nd–3rd trimesters for normal BMI; individualize)

Macronutrients
- Protein: 1.6–1.8 g/kg/day (up to 2.0 g/kg/day is acceptable for advanced lifters if digestion is fine). Distribute across 4–5 feedings with 25–40 g high-quality protein each.
  - Rationale: supports maternal lean mass, fetal growth, and recovery.
- Carbohydrates: 3–5 g/kg/day minimum; up to 5–6 g/kg on heavier training days if appetite/digestion allow.
  - Center carbs pre/post-workout to support performance and limit excessive blood sugar swings.
- Fats: 0.8–1.0 g/kg/day; include omega-3s (DHA/EPA).
  - Don’t push fats so high that they displace protein/carbs needed for training.

Hydration and electrolytes
- Fluids: baseline 30–35 mL/kg/day plus +300–500 mL in pregnancy; add 500–750 mL around training. More in heat.
- Sodium/potassium: lightly salt meals; include potassium-rich foods (potatoes, bananas, dairy, legumes). Consider a low-sugar electrolyte during longer sessions if she sweats heavily.

Pre-/intra-/post-workout fueling
- Pre (60–120 min): 30–60 g carbs + 20–30 g protein; low fiber/fat. Examples: yogurt + fruit; toast + peanut butter + milk; rice cakes + cottage cheese.
- During (if sessions >60 min or in heat): 10–20 g carbs per 30 min via sports drink/chews; sip water/electrolytes.
- Post (within 1–2 h): 30–45 g protein + 60–90 g carbs; include fluids and electrolytes. Examples: turkey wrap + fruit; protein smoothie with milk, oats, berries.

Meal timing structure (example)
- 4–5 meals/snacks/day with even protein distribution.
- Example for 70 kg lifter at ~2,300–2,400 kcal (adjust to her needs):
  - Breakfast: 35 g protein, 60 g carbs, 20 g fat
  - Snack: 25–30 g protein, 30–40 g carbs, 10–15 g fat
  - Lunch: 35–40 g protein, 70–80 g carbs, 20 g fat
  - Pre-train: 20–25 g protein, 30–40 g carbs, low fat
  - Post/dinner: 35–40 g protein, 70–90 g carbs, 15–20 g fat
  - Optional pre-bed: 20–30 g slow protein (Greek yogurt/cottage cheese) if total protein is short

Protein choices
- Lean meats (chicken, turkey, lean beef/pork), fish low in mercury (salmon, sardines, trout) 2–3x/week, eggs/pasteurized egg whites, dairy (Greek yogurt, cottage cheese, milk), tofu/tempeh/edamame, legumes. Whey/pea protein powders can help hit targets; pick third-party tested products.

Carb choices
- Whole grains (oats, rice, quinoa, whole-grain bread/pasta), potatoes/sweet potatoes, fruits, dairy, legumes. Keep fiber moderate to manage GI comfort; choose lower-fiber options pre-training.

Fat choices
- Extra-virgin olive oil, avocado, nuts/seeds, nut butters, dairy, and omega-3 fish; include flax/chia/walnuts if fish intake is low.

Micronutrient priorities
- Prenatal vitamin/mineral: as prescribed by OB.
- Iron: monitor ferritin; include heme iron (lean red meat) 2–3x/week, pair non-heme sources with vitamin C; separate iron supplements from calcium.
- Calcium: ~1,000 mg/day; dairy/fortified alternatives, leafy greens.
- Vitamin D: ensure sufficiency; supplement per labs (often 1,000–2,000 IU/day; defer to OB).
- Iodine: ~220 mcg/day; prenatal typically covers; include dairy/iodized salt.
- Choline: ~450 mg/day; eggs, lean meats, dairy; consider choline bitartrate if intake is low (confirm with OB).
- Folate: prenatal covers; include leafy greens/legumes.
- DHA/EPA: ~300–500 mg DHA/day via fish or prenatal with DHA; choose low-mercury fish.
- Magnesium: food-first (pumpkin seeds, legumes, dark chocolate); consider 200–300 mg magnesium glycinate at night if cramps/sleep issues (per OB).

Food safety and pregnancy-specific guidance
- Avoid high-mercury fish (shark, swordfish, king mackerel, tilefish); limit albacore tuna.
- No unpasteurized dairy/juices; avoid undercooked meats/eggs, deli meats unless heated to steaming.
- Limit caffeine to ≤200 mg/day.
- Alcohol: avoid.
- Wash produce thoroughly; practice safe food handling.

Managing common symptoms
- Nausea/aversions: small frequent meals; cold foods; ginger/peppermint; bland starch + protein combos.
- Reflux: smaller meals, avoid late high-fat meals; elevate head of bed; choose lower-acid foods around evening.
- Constipation: fluids; 25–35 g/day fiber from fruits, veg, whole grains, legumes; add prunes/kiwi; consider psyllium; walk daily.
- Leg cramps: check hydration, magnesium, potassium intake.

- Snack: Smoothie (milk, whey/pea protein, banana, spinach, oats, peanut butter).
- Lunch: Salmon, quinoa, roasted vegetables, olive oil drizzle; side fruit.
- Pre-training: Rice cakes with cottage cheese and jam; water/electrolyte.
- Post/dinner: Turkey taco bowl (lean turkey, rice, black beans, avocado, salsa, cheese).
- Pre-bed (optional): Cottage cheese with kiwi.

Supplement checklist (confirm with OB)
- Prenatal multivitamin with iron, iodine, folate
- DHA (if not covered in prenatal): 300–500 mg/day
- Vitamin D based on labs
- Creatine monohydrate 3–5 g/day appears safe in healthy pregnancies in emerging evidence, but use only with OB approval
- Magnesium glycinate 200–300 mg at night if needed
- Protein powder to help meet targets (third-party tested)

Monitoring and adjustments
- Track 3–4 days of intake and symptoms during Week 1–2; adjust calories by ±100–150 kcal to keep energy stable, training recovery solid, and weight gain on target per OB.
- Aim for consistent protein at each meal and carbs around training.
- Use a simple hunger/energy/sleep/stress log to guide tweaks.

This plan keeps nutrients high, supports lean mass, and fits the training program while respecting pregnancy-specific needs.

Here’s a pregnancy-safe cardio plan that complements the 12-week strength program and supports cardiovascular fitness, recovery, and healthy weight gain while preserving lean mass.

Global cardio guidelines
- Frequency: 3–5 days/week total movement; 2–3 structured cardio sessions + optional light recovery walks.
- Intensity anchor: Talk test and RPE 3–6/10. Keep most work at conversational pace. Avoid max efforts and overheating.
- Duration: 20–35 minutes per session (can be split into 2 x 10–15 min if needed).
- Surfaces/modes: Low-impact and stable—incline treadmill walk, stationary bike, elliptical, rowing machine (if bump allows), deep-water walking, sled pushes (light), stepper at low heights. Avoid contact sports, high fall risk, and supine intervals.
- Temperature/hydration: Cool, ventilated space; hydrate before/during/after; consider a fan.
- Warning signs to stop: dizziness, chest pain, vaginal bleeding, leaking fluid, painful contractions, unusual shortness of breath, calf pain/swelling, pelvic or pubic symphysis pain, decreased fetal movement. If symptoms occur, stop and consult OB.

Structure across 12 weeks
- Phase 1 (Weeks 1–4, ~20–23 weeks): Build consistency at low-to-moderate intensity.
- Phase 2 (Weeks 5–8, ~24–27 weeks): Maintain volume, introduce gentle tempo changes.
- Phase 3 (Weeks 9–12, ~28–31 weeks): Prioritize comfort; shorter bouts or more frequent low-intensity sessions.

Weekly template
- Option A (3x/week structured): Mon 25–30 min, Wed 20–25 min, Sat 25–35 min
- Option B (2x/week structured + 2 short walks): Tues 25–30 min, Fri 25–30 min, plus 2 x 15–20 min easy walks on other days
- Pair lower-demand cardio days with upper-body or rest days; keep hard cardio 24 h away from hardest lower-body strength if fatigue is high.

Phase 1 details (Weeks 1–4)
Goal: Establish steady-state aerobic base.
- Session type: Steady aerobic (Z1–Z2, RPE 3–5)
- Duration: Start 20–25 min; add 2–3 min each week as tolerated.
- Example sessions:
  - Incline treadmill walk: 3-min easy warm-up, then 18–25 min at 2–5% incline, brisk but conversational, 3-min cool-down.
  - Stationary bike: 5-min easy, 15–20 min at 60–70% of perceived max effort (cadence smooth), 3–5 min cool-down.
  - Elliptical: 5-min easy, 15–20 min steady, 3–5 min cool-down.
- Optional finishers: 4–6 x 20–30 s “form strides” on the bike or elliptical at RPE 6 with 60–90 s easy between, only if no pelvic pressure or symptoms.

Phase 2 details (Weeks 5–8)
Goal: Keep volume, add gentle variety/tempo without spikes.
- Session mix: 1 steady aerobic + 1 cadence/tempo session + 1 recovery walk or pool session.
- Cadence/tempo session (example on bike/elliptical/rower):
  - Warm-up 6 min easy
  - 6–8 x 1 min at RPE 6 (comfortably hard, still able to speak short phrases) + 2 min easy spin
  - Cool-down 4–5 min
  - Total 24–30 min
- Steady session: 25–30 min Z2, conversational.
- Recovery session: 20–25 min easy walk or deep-water walk.
- Notes:
  - Avoid running/jogging if new to it during pregnancy; if she was a consistent runner pre-pregnancy and remains symptom-free, substitute low-impact intervals on a 0–2% incline: 8–12 x 1 min brisk/2 min easy, staying RPE ≤6 and watching pelvic floor symptoms.

Phase 3 details (Weeks 9–12)
Goal: Comfort and frequency over intensity; manage balance and pelvic pressure.
- Use machines or pool for support; break longer sessions into shorter bouts if needed.
- Session options:
  - Pool: 25–30 min deep-water walk or aqua-jog belt, steady conversational pace.
  - Bike: 5-min warm-up, 4 x 4 min at RPE 5–6 with 2 min easy between, finish with 5–8 min easy (total 30–35 min).
  - Treadmill walk: 5 min easy, 15–20 min steady at modest incline, 3–5 min cool-down.
- If pelvic or low-back discomfort increases: prioritize pool sessions, recumbent bike, or shorter 10–15 min walks after meals (2–3x/day).

Weekly progression example
- Week 1: 2 sessions x 20–25 min steady
- Week 2: 3 sessions x 20–25 min steady
- Week 3: 3 sessions x 22–28 min (optionally add light 20–30 s pick-ups)
- Week 4: Deload—2 sessions x 20–22 min easy
- Week 5: 1 steady 25–30 min, 1 cadence session 24–28 min, 1 recovery walk 20–25 min
- Week 6: Maintain or +2–3 min total per session
- Week 7: Repeat Week 6 or add 1 interval to cadence session if RPE stays ≤6
- Week 8: Deload—reduce duration by ~20%
- Week 9: 2–3 sessions, prioritize pool/recumbent bike, 20–30 min each
- Week 10: Maintain frequency; keep RPE 3–5 most of the time
- Week 11: If energy good, 1 bike session with 4 x 4 min at RPE 5–6; others easy
- Week 12: Deload—2 easy sessions 20–25 min, plus gentle walks as desired

Integration with strength days
- On strength days: Keep cardio easy (10–20 min cool-down walk/bike) or do cardio on separate days.
- Post-leg day: Choose low-impact (bike, pool) at easy pace.
- Fuel: Include carbs and fluids pre/post; electrolyte if sweating notably.

Pelvic floor and comfort considerations
- Monitor for heaviness, leakage, or coning. If present, reduce intensity, choose more supported modes (bike/pool), and shorten bouts.
- Favor shorter strides, lower inclines if pubic symphysis discomfort appears.
- Keep posture “ribs over pelvis,” light arm swing or supported handlebars to avoid excessive trunk extension.

Optional low-intensity extras
- NEAT: 6–10k steps/day if comfortable, broken into short walks, especially 10–15 min after meals to aid glycemic control and digestion.
- Mobility breath walks: 10–15 min nasal-breathing walks on rest days to aid recovery.

This cardio plan keeps intensity moderate, supports aerobic fitness and recovery, and aligns with pregnancy safety while preserving lean mass alongside the strength and nutrition plans.

Goal: Strong training feel via top sets, clusters/EMOMs, density blocks; manage posture and symmetry; keep RPE ceilings.

  - Day A Lower: Hatfield squat to box—Top 1x4 @RPE 8; back-offs 3x4 @7. DB RDL 4x6 @7–8; Step-downs 3x10/side @7; Density 8–10 min: Cable pull-through 10 + Banded lateral walk 12/side.

  - Strength: Progress top sets 2.5–5% if clean; maintain structure.

  - Cardio Session 1—6x2 min @RPE 6–7 + 2 min easy; Session 2—Z2 25–30; Session 3—Recovery.

Phase 3 (Weeks 9–12): Comfort, stability, expression (gestational ~28–31)
Goal: Keep strength quality, reduce axial peaks, favor machines/support; prepare for peak-style Week 12 without true maxing.
- Week 9
  - Day A Lower: Leg press 4x8 @6–7; DB RDL with wall support 4x6–8; Step-up low box 3x8/side; Cable pull-through or banded hip thrust 3x12; Standing Pallof 3x10/side.

  - Maintain/microload 1–2% if symptom-free; swap step-ups for single-leg press if balance wanes; add adductor/abductor machine 2x12 each if desired.

  - Day A: Leg press 5x6 @7; Wall-supported DB RDL 4x8; Reverse lunge 3x8/side; Pull-through 3x12.

- Week 12 Peak-style (no 1RMs)
  - Day A “heavy exposures”: Hatfield or Leg Press—2–3 singles @RPE 7–8 (clean speed); Back-off 2x4 @~80% of day’s single @RPE ~7. Trap bar blocks 3x2 @RPE 7; Split squat 2x8/side @7; Pallof 2x10/side.

  - Optional cap-set after A1 on Days A/B: 1 set at a load you could do 8–10 reps; stop at 6 reps or RPE 8 to estimate e1RM safely.
  - Core (light): 90/90 breathing 2x5; Standing Pallof 2x8/side; Side-lying TVA 2x5 breaths.
  - Cardio: Deload—2 easy Z1–Z2 sessions 20–25 min; gentle walks.
  - Post-peak: 3–4 easy recovery days before resuming.

Cardio summary (weeks 1–12)
- Phase 1: 2–3x/week steady 20–30 min (talk-test).
- Phase 2: 2 structured + 1 recovery
  - W5: 8x1 min @RPE 6–7 + 2 min easy; Z2 25–30; Recovery 20–25.
  - W6: 6x2 min @RPE 6–7 + 2 min easy; Z2; Recovery.

Core summary (rotate per weeks above; 2–3 drills post-lift, 2–3 sets, RPE 6–7)
- Staples: 90/90 breathing; Pallof variations; Incline dead bug; Bird-dog (short lever); Side bridge on bench; Tall/half-kneeling chops/lifts; Suitcase carries; High-incline bear hover; Marching cable row iso.
- Rules: Avoid supine/sit-ups/rollouts; stop at first sign of coning/heaviness; prioritize quality and breathing.

Pressing emphasis summary
- Weekly: One strong incline press (barbell/DB/machine) with top set/back-offs in Phase 2; one landmine or seated DB press; push-up/cable fly accessories as tolerated.
- RPE ceilings: Top sets to 8 in Phase 2; maintain 6–7 elsewhere. Swap to machine if arching/balance uncomfortable.

Nutrition summary for lean mass and pregnancy support
- Calories: +250–350 kcal/day in 2nd tri; +350–450 kcal/day as 3rd tri approaches; adjust ±100–150 kcal based on OB-guided weight gain, energy, and performance.
- Macros:
  - Protein: 1.6–1.8 g/kg/day (up to 2.0 if tolerated), 4–5 feedings of 25–40 g.
  - Carbs: 3–5 g/kg/day baseline; up to 5–6 g/kg on heavier training days.
  - Fats: 0.8–1.0 g/kg/day; include DHA/EPA.
- Peri-workout: 30–60 g carbs + 20–30 g protein pre; fluids/electrolytes and optional 10–20 g carbs per 30 min during longer/hot sessions; 30–45 g protein + 60–90 g carbs post.
- Micronutrients/supplements (per OB): Prenatal with iron/iodine/folate; DHA 300–500 mg if not in prenatal; Vitamin D per labs; calcium ~1,000 mg/day; choline ~450 mg/day; creatine 3–5 g/day only with OB approval; magnesium glycinate 200–300 mg at night if needed.
- Hydration: 30–35 mL/kg/day + 300–500 mL in pregnancy; +500–750 mL around training; light electrolytes as needed.
- Food safety: Low-mercury fish; avoid unpasteurized foods/undercooked meats; caffeine ≤200 mg/day; no alcohol.

Recovery and modification keys
- Sleep 7–9 h; side-lying with pillows. Cool environment; avoid overheating.
- Shoe support as laxity increases. Narrow stance/shorter strides if pubic symphysis pain; prefer leg press/box squats.
- Red flags: dizziness, bleeding, leaking fluid, chest pain, calf swelling, severe headache, painful contractions, unusual SOB, decreased fetal movement, sharp pelvic/pubic pain—stop and refer.

Outcome
- She maintains meaningful strength with a strong training feel in Phase 2, preserves lean mass, and progresses safely through 28–31 weeks. Week 12 provides a satisfying peak without 1RM risk, setting clear benchmarks for the next block. Adjust day-to-day by RPE, symptoms, and OB guidance.
